_comment: Benchmark constants v3. The reference numbers the build still reads, after the quartile-lever model was retired on 2026-09-23 (docs/DATA_MODEL.md #3): the basket of comparable launches is the benchmark for every volume and rate. What stays: order_split (the medians split a display group's target across its raw channels, since the panel is grouped), cost_per_purchase (the Median is the default price of a paid unit; a release can type its own), the entry-to-order rates, cannibalisation 0.2 (the LE standard per the workbook's spend rules), the framing defaults, the budget sense check, the spend rules and the cost-curve priors. Transcribed from the 2026-08-28 LAUNCH PERFORMANCE OVERVIEW (recomputed panel; quartiles over the historical release panel). See docs/DATA_MODEL.md #4 for provenance. Currency EUR: the spend and the prices these were computed from are Meta's and Shopify's euro figures.

order_split._meaning: channel share of unadjusted draw+preorder units, Low=P25 / Medium=median / High=P75; the build reads the Medium column only, renormalised inside each display group, to split a group's basket target across its channels

cost_per_purchase._meaning: EUR per paid unit, quartiles over the paid campaigns on file; Median prices the paid budget only when a release has no cost_per_purchase of its own and fewer than three of its basket's launches have a cost per paid unit on file (etl/build.py cost_per_purchase_for: the release's figure, else the basket's median, else this)

spend_rules.cpe_daily_drift_note: Retired 2026-09-28: cost per entry no longer drifts with the calendar. It rises with the campaign's spend so far (cpe_wearout), which the 2026-09-28 fit on 47 campaigns / 783 campaign-days preferred to a straight drift a day (deviance 1375 against 1456; the straight drift read 3.6% a day). The workbook's 5/7/10% a day by third is kept in cpe_daily_drift_by_third_workbook for reference: it is the cost rise along the workbook's own ramping spend path, which the spend-so-far curve now prices.
spend_rules._source: The cumulative-ROI bands (0.9 / 1.3), the 30% cap and the 10% dead band are the TL template's 'ROI / SPEND RULES - DO NOT CHANGE' block (LAUNCH PERFORMANCE OVERVIEW, TL_Template rows 416-428), applied to LE for want of a fuller LE block. The LE template's own SPEND RULES (rows 284-299) are: decrease/increase steps of 10%, max increase per day 2.0, target ROI AA 1.1, a 30% decrease on a zero-conversion day, a 100% decrease (pause) after 3 days of zero conversion, and 'Expected Increase in Spend (%)' 5/7/10 by third - a typed constant with no derivation, read by row 206 as the daily growth of the forecast cost per unit. Neither tab derives its drift from data; the TL tab labels its 2.16%/day '(assumed)'.

cpe_spend_elasticity_note: Prior for the within-campaign elasticity of cost per entry to the day's budget, net of the wear-out on spend so far and the close's lift: doubling the day's budget makes an entry about 23% dearer at 0.30. Set on 2026-10-27 from etl/analysis/cpe_elasticity_challenge.py rather than the plain fit, which reads low: the budget is raised after cheap days and cheapness persists, so the plain fit (0.15 on 47 campaigns / 814 campaign-days with spend over 20 up to the close; 0.08 on the 42 / 705 of the 2026-09-28 fit) sees big days that were cheap because they were made big on cheap days. Readings that sidestep that: consecutive days alone 0.27 +/- 0.05; two-day windows around budget steps of 30%+ 0.36 on 194 rises and 0.33 on 81 cuts; a backtest predicting the rest of each campaign from the spend it had misses least at 0.25 to 0.35 (30% against 36% at the old pair) with no bias (+8% there). Meta's own price barely moves (impressions on the day's budget: elasticity 0.08); the penalty is in what an impression is worth on a bigger day. Entries do not lag the spend that bought them (yesterday's budget adds 0.03), so same-day readings stand. The width, cpe_spend_elasticity_sd 0.10, spans the readings. A campaign with cpe_fit_min_days of history gets its own elasticity fitted and shrunk to this prior by precision (etl/build.py campaign_cost_terms). Set to 0 to price the day's level flat.
cpe_wearout_note: Prior for the wear-out w: each doubling of what a campaign has spent so far makes its next entry 2^w times dearer, read as (1 + spend so far / cpe_wearout_k)^w. The plain fit (etl/analysis/cpe_elasticity.py, 2026-10-27, 47 campaigns / 814 campaign-days up to the close, with the close's lift): 0.202 +/- 0.016, an entry 15% dearer (13% fewer entries a euro) with each doubling; between-campaign sd 0.13 (cpe_wearout_sd). The 2026-09-28 fit on 42 / 705 read 0.240 +/- 0.021. The backtest in cpe_elasticity_challenge.py is flat over 0.15 to 0.25 at the elasticity prior. K = EUR 100: the fit is flat below it and worsens above (deviance 1478 at 100, 1517 at 1,000). The exploratory fits on the sign-ups the draw campaigns bring and on link clicks across every campaign, sign-up campaigns included, wear out alike. A campaign with cpe_fit_min_days of history gets its own wear-out fitted and shrunk to this prior by precision (etl/build.py campaign_cost_terms).
cpe_close_lift_note: The close's lift: how many times the entries a euro buys on the draw's close day ([0]) and the day before ([1]), as the deadline pulls people in, on top of the spend-so-far curve. Same fit: x1.53 (95% x1.26 to x1.87) and x1.40 (x1.07 to x1.83); the day before those reads x1.07 +/- 0.14 and later days nothing. It is the final days' own paid sign-ups entering at once, not credit deferred from earlier paid sign-ups coming back after an email (an entry is attributed to the channel of the session the person signed up in, and a draw started and not finished counts as signing up): at account level 87% of the final two days' paid entries signed up on those days, and 0.3% of the paid sign-ups who had not entered by then did so then; within a campaign a euro buys x1.15 as many sign-ups on the close day and each is x1.22 as likely to enter (etl/analysis/close_rush.py, aggregates only). The forward path lifts its last two days by these and takes the lift out of the trailing window it is anchored on; each campaign's own terms are fitted with the lift held at these (etl/build.py CostPath, campaign_cost_terms). The ROI floor reads the price at the close before the lift, the path's worst day. cpe_close_lift_applied false runs the path on the curve alone, the fit keeping the lift; [] drops it from the fit as well.
cpe_growth_factor_note: Superseded: the forward cost per entry follows the campaign's spend so far (cpe_wearout) and the day's budget (cpe_spend_elasticity), one path for the paid projection, the ROI chart, the budget and the ROI floor (etl/build.py CostPath). Kept for reference only.
